clue.text: Omission concerning location, it's said

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money

indicators.note: it's said tells us the word for location is to be taken by its sound, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone describes a gap in the record about where something happened, according to hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' applies only to the word for location: SITE as heard becomes SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a failure to notice something, a slip or thing left out.

clue.text: Come up with chest, lid missing

indicators.note: lid missing says the chest loses its top letter

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: Someone produces a chest that has lost its lid.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer is to put forward or propose, to produce something for consideration.

clue.text: On the Road, Kerouac's second? True, no kidding

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the name Kerouac
kidding suggests the words are not to be taken straight, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A question about Kerouac's road novel and its sequel, answered seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no kidding' looks like one phrase, but 'no' is part of the letters mixed by 'kidding'. The definition is the title of Kerouac's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: En route is French for on the way, travelling.

clue.text: Rest bringing in fish, working to close a deal

indicators.note: bringing in means the rest word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to sit is to rest
hake is a fish
on means working, as in switched on

explanation.surface: A break brings in a catch, and the work seals a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Shake on it is the idiom for agreeing terms with a handshake.

clue.text: Strong growth of opinion in field of research on expansion

parts.note: ground is an area of study, as in covering new ground
a swell is an increase or expansion

explanation.surface: A rising view in one area of study about growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a rising tide of public feeling, a build-up of support.

clue.text: Bill, in club, keeled over

indicators.note: keeled over means toppled, so in a down clue the club is turned upside down

parts.note: a bat is a club

explanation.surface: Bill collapsed at his club.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is a bill run up, as in picking up the tab.

clue.text: Rebuke duke deserved

parts.note: to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: A duke got the telling-off he had coming to him.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE in the sense of scold is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rated has been judged worthy of a ranking, so merited or earned.

clue.text: Cap removed from toy gun

indicators.note: cap removed means the toy word loses its top letter

parts.note: to trifle with is to toy with

explanation.surface: A cap has been taken off a toy pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' suggests the paper cap of a toy gun, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm.

clue.text: Pointed towards, in addition, answer in 25

parts.note: too means as well or in addition

indicators.note: in places the answer letter within the name from clue 25

parts.note: 25 refers to the answer of clue 25 down, the girl's name

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that points somewhere else in the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To take aim at something is to point a weapon at it, directing it at a target.

clue.text: Intimate group after ultimate in food and service

indicators.note: after places the inner group behind the letter from food
ultimate in picks the final letter of food

parts.note: inner means private or intimate, as in an inner circle
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A close circle follows the best in food and service.
explanation.definitionFit: A service is a full set of matching tableware, such as a dinner set.

clue.text: Jumble taken from charitable event held in Portuguese resort

indicators.note: held in signals the charity event sitting inside the resort's name

parts.note: Faro is a resort town on Portugal's Algarve coast
a rag is a British student fundraising event for charity, often a rag week

explanation.surface: A muddle emerges from a fundraiser staged at a holiday town in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is a British university students' charity drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or hotchpotch of things.

clue.text: Expert has nothing on clown

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert, as in film buff
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A specialist is wearing nothing in front of a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a fool or jester who acts ridiculously for laughs.

clue.text: Wheel shows this as rake scoops in grand?

indicators.note: scoops in suggests the rake gathering the grand into himself, one piece inside another

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a rake
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: At the roulette table a gambler rakes in a thousand as the wheel spins.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the roulette wheel: its pockets show red or black, in French rouge or noir.
explanation.definitionFit: On a roulette wheel the red numbers are called rouge, the French word for red.

clue.text: Name surprisingly moderate building by the Seine

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of moderate end up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone names a modest structure on the banks of the Paris river, to general surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral of Notre-Dame stands on an island in the Seine in Paris.

clue.text: Sudden acceleration up front, see, affected leader in Derby

indicators.note: affected means changed, so the letters are worked into new order
leader in takes the first letter of Derby

explanation.surface: A racehorse leading the Derby puts on a burst of speed at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of speed is the ability to accelerate quickly, especially of a horse.

clue.text: Signal for action in botanical gardens, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks the gardens' name as something spoken, standing for a word of the same sound

parts.note: Kew Gardens in west London is the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: Something at the botanic gardens prompts activity, people report.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is Britain's famous botanic garden in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt, as given to an actor telling them to begin.

clue.text: One who gave warnings misinterpreted as canards

indicators.note: misinterpreted suggests the words are read wrongly, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A prophet's warnings were wrongly taken as false rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is close to an &lit: her true prophecies were never believed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra was the Trojan prophetess fated to foretell disaster and never be believed.

clue.text: Seer's crazy schemes rejected, using common sense about this

indicators.note: about means the common-sense word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: nous is British slang for practical good sense

indicators.note: rejected means the crazy schemes are sent back, read from the end

parts.note: mad means crazy
arts are wiles or schemes, as in arts and wiles

explanation.surface: A prophet dismisses wild plans and relies on plain good sense about this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer's' is read as 'Seer is'; 'crazy schemes' looks like one phrase but gives two pieces. NOUS is British slang for practical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The 16th-century French astrologer is the most famous prophet of all.

clue.text: Taking off a corollary

definitions.meaning: subtracting something, as an amount removed from pay
a conclusion drawn by reasoning from what is known

explanation.surface: Removing an inference.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a subtraction from a total and a logical inference.

clue.text: Instant divorce supporter

parts.note: a split is a separation or divorce
a second backs someone, as in a duel or boxing match

explanation.surface: A quickie divorce and someone backing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is the briefest moment of time, an instant.

clue.text: Library's head brought in academic

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of library

parts.note: earned means brought in, as money

explanation.surface: A senior librarian was recruited from the university staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned means scholarly, showing great knowledge from study.

clue.text: Malicious gossip bringing article into court

indicators.note: into places the article inside the court's letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Spiteful chatter leads to a newspaper piece being produced in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is a spiteful woman given to catty remarks, a scandalmonger.

clue.text: Chapter on opening a place for nuns

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A religious chapter meets to open a nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a house where a community of nuns lives.

clue.text: A girl is crossing lines in plant

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
L stands for line, so two Ls for lines

explanation.surface: A young woman walks across some lines in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaryllis is a bulb plant with large trumpet-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Poet sure to receive a first from Trinity

indicators.note: to receive means the yes word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: sure as a reply means yes

indicators.note: first from takes the opening letter of Trinity

explanation.surface: A poet is certain to get a top degree from Trinity College.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a first' suggests a first-class degree, but 'a' is a letter and 'first from' picks T.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Passage about North American lake

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A route near a lake on the American continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway, a channel for boats or a duct in the body.

clue.text: Large Italian male, supple

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and It
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A big Italian man who is agile.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and graceful in movement.

clue.text: Study model kingdom

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
a mark is a model or version, as in a Mark II car

explanation.surface: A sample realm to be examined.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian monarchy, one of Europe's oldest kingdoms.

clue.text: Girl shown in ski mask

indicators.note: shown in says the name can be seen inside the words ski mask

explanation.surface: A young woman appears in a balaclava.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim is a girl's name, as in Kim Basinger.

clue.text: I had contracted to appear in competition easy to see

indicators.note: to appear in means the shortened form shows up within the competition

parts.note: an event is a competition
I had shortened gives I'd, the letters ID

explanation.surface: Someone signed up to take part in a contest that is plainly visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means obvious or plain, clear to anyone looking.

clue.text: Right-hand men in a team lacking leadership succeeded

indicators.note: lacking leadership means the team word loses its first letter

parts.note: a side is a team
S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Deputies in a leaderless team went on to triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Aides are assistants, the trusted helpers of someone in charge.

clue.text: Parisian salesgirl in motorway eating area

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a dinette is a small dining area

explanation.surface: A French shop assistant at a service station cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Paris shop girl, especially a young milliner's assistant.
